# Rule Enforcement Convention

A convention that lives only in prose is caught at review, one violation at a time, by whoever
happens to read carefully. The same convention written as a selector is caught while it is being
typed — but only if the failure says which convention was broken. `Using 'no-restricted-syntax' is
not allowed` teaches nobody anything, so the first person it inconveniences turns it off.

This is what goes into the house block that [config-convention.md](./config-convention.md) places
last.

## Scope

Applies to encoding this kit's conventions in an ESLint config.

Does **not** apply to:

- The conventions a linter cannot check — see
  [§ What the linter is not for](#what-the-linter-is-not-for). Those stay prose and stay owned by
  their own rule files.
- Framework recommended sets, which are adopted whole rather than re-derived.
- Replacing any rule. A selector is a reminder of a rule, never the rule itself.

## The selectors live in one module

Put every house selector in a module of its own — `agentkit.js` — and have the presets import it. A
selector written inline in a preset is invisible to the other presets and gets re-typed slightly
differently in the next one.

```js
// CORRECT — agentkit.js owns the selectors, and names the ones that get relaxed
export const STEP_NAMED_LOCAL_SYNTAX = { selector: '…', message: '…' };

export const AGENTKIT_RESTRICTED_SYNTAX = [
  { selector: "CatchClause[param.name='err']", message: '…' },
  STEP_NAMED_LOCAL_SYNTAX,
];

export const AGENTKIT_STYLE_RULES = {
  'no-restricted-syntax': ['error', ...AGENTKIT_RESTRICTED_SYNTAX],
};

// WRONG — a selector typed into base.js, then typed again into react.js
rules: { 'no-restricted-syntax': ['error', { selector: "CatchClause[param.name='err']", … }] },
```

Any entry a scope will need to lift gets its own exported name, so lifting it is a `filter` on a
named thing rather than a copy of the array with one entry quietly missing.

## Every message names the rule it enforces

The message is the only part of the failure a reader sees. It states the rule, the section, and the
form to write instead.

```js
// CORRECT — names the rule, then shows the shape that passes
message:
  'naming-convention §Locals: name the entity the binding holds, not the step that produced it — ' +
  'createdCustomer, existingIdempotencyKey, customerRows.',

// WRONG — the reader learns only that something is banned
message: 'Do not use this variable name.',
```

## What maps onto what

The conventions below are mechanical, so they are enforced mechanically. Nothing else in this table
is discretionary — a project on this profile encodes all of it.

| Convention                                                                                                                                   | How it is caught                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [naming-convention § Locals](../../core/naming-convention.md#locals)                                                                         | `VariableDeclarator[id.name=/^(created\|updated\|existing\|found\|result\|record\|row\|item\|data\|values\|obj\|node)$/]` |
| [naming-convention § Abbreviations](../../core/naming-convention.md#abbreviations)                                                           | `CatchClause[param.name='err']`                                                                                           |
| [verb-convention § The verb carries no qualifiers](../../core/verb-convention.md#the-verb-carries-no-qualifiers)                             | `MethodDefinition[key.name=/By[A-Z]/]` and `MethodDefinition[key.name=/(OrThrow\|OrNull\|OrFail\|Async)$/]`               |
| [verb-convention § Verbs](../../core/verb-convention.md#verbs)                                                                               | `MethodDefinition[key.name=/^(list\|fetch\|load\|save\|insert\|purge\|destroy)[A-Z]/]`                                    |
| [logging-convention](../../core/logging-convention.md#message-shape)                                                                         | `Property[key.name='err']`                                                                                                |
| [nested-access-convention § Read it once](../../core/nested-access-convention.md#read-it-once)                                               | `MemberExpression[optional=true] > MemberExpression[optional=true]`                                                       |
| [nested-access-convention § A fallback is a destructure default](../../core/nested-access-convention.md#a-fallback-is-a-destructure-default) | `LogicalExpression[operator='??'][right.raw!='null'] > ChainExpression.left`, and the `<container> ?? {}` selector        |
| [import-convention](../../core/import-convention.md#principle)                                                                               | `no-restricted-imports` banning the groups `['../*', '../../*', '../../../*']`                                            |
| [typescript](../../core/typescript.md)                                                                                                       | `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, `no-non-null-assertion`, `no-unused-vars` with `argsIgnorePattern: '^_'`            |
| [statement-convention](../../core/statement-convention.md#one-statement-one-job)                                                             | `@stylistic/padding-line-between-statements`                                                                              |
| braces and arrow bodies                                                                                                                      | `curly: ['error', 'all']`, `arrow-body-style: ['error', 'always']`                                                        |

The `?? {}` and the fused-fallback selectors are the two that repay reading twice, because both
describe a shape rather than a name:

```js
{
  selector: "LogicalExpression[operator='??'][right.raw!='null'] > ChainExpression.left",
  message:
    'nested-access-convention: `?.` fused to a `??` fallback — read the path once into a named ' +
    'local, or destructure the field with a default. Only `?? null` at a boundary stays.',
},
{
  selector:
    "VariableDeclarator[id.type='ObjectPattern'] > LogicalExpression[operator='??'] > " +
    'ObjectExpression.right[properties.length=0]',
  message:
    'nested-access-convention: `<container> ?? {}` invents an object to read a field off — guard ' +
    'the container instead.',
},
```

`[right.raw!='null']` is the guard that keeps `email: account.email ?? null` legal at a boundary,
where it restates `undefined` rather than supplying a value. Drop the guard and every correct
boundary read reports, which is the fastest way to get the whole rule switched off.

## Relax with a scoped override, never an inline disable

A place where a rule should not apply is a fact about that place, so it belongs in the config, where
one reader can see every exception at once. `// eslint-disable-next-line` scatters the same decision
across the files that happen to hit it.

```js
// CORRECT — tests may bind `result`; every other selector still applies
{
  files: ['**/*.test.ts', '**/*.test.tsx', '**/tests/**'],
  rules: {
    'no-restricted-syntax': [
      'error',
      ...AGENTKIT_RESTRICTED_SYNTAX.filter((entry) => {
        return entry !== STEP_NAMED_LOCAL_SYNTAX;
      }),
    ],
  },
}

// CORRECT — exactly one file may import the thing everything else reaches through a client
{
  files: ['src/libs/auth-client.ts'],
  rules: { 'no-restricted-imports': ['error', { patterns: [...RELATIVE_PARENT_IMPORTS.patterns] }] },
}

// WRONG — the exception is now invisible from the config, and the next file copies it
// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax
const result = await this.customerRepository.createCustomer(payload);
```

Re-declaring the rule for a narrower `files` glob replaces it there rather than merging, so the
override states the full set it wants, built from the shared array.

## Architectural boundaries are import bans

A layering rule — only repositories touch the tables, only one module talks to the vendor SDK — is
enforced the same way, as a `no-restricted-imports` pattern whose message names the convention it
comes from.

Where the ban should stop values but let types through, use the typescript-eslint variant for
`allowTypeImports`, and turn the core rule **off** in that same block so the two do not both report:

```js
{
  files: ['src/**/*.ts'],
  ignores: ['src/repositories/**', 'src/database/**'],
  rules: {
    'no-restricted-imports': 'off',
    '@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports': [
      'error',
      {
        patterns: [
          ...RELATIVE_PARENT_IMPORTS.patterns,
          {
            group: ['@database/schemas*'],
            allowTypeImports: true,
            message: 'query-convention: only repositories import the tables — go through a repository.',
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
}
```

## What the linter is not for

Some conventions have no syntactic tell, and a selector that guesses at one produces false positives
until somebody deletes the rule — taking the true positives with it. Leave these to the rule files
and to review:

- [comment-convention.md](../../core/comment-convention.md) — a comment is syntax, but "the code
  should have said it" is not.
- [verb-convention.md](../../core/verb-convention.md) — that `get` throws and `find` returns `null`
  is about the body, not the name.
- [vocabulary-convention.md](../../core/vocabulary-convention.md) — whether an argument is really a
  payload, a filter or a query.
- [minimal-surface-convention.md](../../core/minimal-surface-convention.md) — whether a parameter
  has a reader.
- [testing.md](../../core/testing.md) — whether a test pins a behaviour or an implementation
  detail.

The split is not a gap to be closed later. A selector earns its place by being right every time it
fires; anything less belongs in prose.

## NEVER Do

- Write a selector inline in a preset instead of in the shared selector module.
- Ship a restricted-syntax message that does not name the convention and the form to write instead.
- Use `// eslint-disable` in a source file where a scoped `files` override in the config would say
  the same thing.
- Drop the `?? null` guard from the fused-fallback selector — a correct boundary read must not
  report.
- Let `no-restricted-imports` and `@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports` both run over the same
  files.
- Encode a semantic convention as a selector because it was nearly expressible.
